question.text: The crystalline form of borax has

options.text: Tetra nuclear <math><msup><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> unit
All boron atoms in the same plane

Equal number of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> hybridized boron atoms

solution.text:
(A) Having B4O5OH42- tetra nuclear (boron) unit.
(B) All boron atoms not in same plane.
(C) Two boron are sp2 hybridised and two boron are sp3 hybridised.
(D) One terminal hydroxide per boron atom is present.
